entities.name: Perry Smith
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Perry Smith (1783–1852) was an American Democratic politician from Connecticut who served in the U.S. Senate (1837–1843) during the Van Buren and Tyler administrations — the Panic of 1837 and its political aftermath. As a Connecticut Democrat, Smith represented a minority position in the most reliably Federalist and then Whig state in New England — Connecticut's Standing Order tradition made it one of the most Federalist-friendly states, and Connecticut Democrats were often fighting against the dominant Whig political culture.

His Senate tenure coincided with the most economically disruptive period of the antebellum era — the Panic of 1837's depression and the political battles over the Independent Treasury that Van Buren and his supporters advocated as the Democratic response.

Connecticut's manufacturing economy — the early industrialization that was transforming the state — created complex economic interests that shaped Smith's Senate position.

He was a lawyer before entering politics.
